name: Base Model to Assistant
strandNote: Optional for every role. Research roles that train or evaluate language models, and anyone who must trust a model's score.
description: Turn a base model into an assistant with fine-tuning and preferences, and measure it honestly.

requires.why: Fine-tunes the tiny GPT with its own training loop, changing only which tokens count.
RLHF is a policy gradient on the language model, with REINFORCE and a baseline.
A Bradley-Terry reward model is a logistic regression on score differences.
Corrects for many benchmarks and comparisons, as for many strategies tried.
Contamination is leakage: the training data already holds the test items.

lessonNames.l1-base-or-assistant: A base model is not an assistant
lessonNames.l15-has-it-seen-the-test: Has the model seen the test?

lessonObjectives.l1-base-or-assistant: Explain what a base model does with a question, and what fine-tuning data must teach it.
lessonObjectives.l2-the-chat-format: Write a chat template that turns a conversation into tokens with role markers.
lessonObjectives.l3-loss-masking: Code a loss mask so only the assistant's tokens are trained on.
lessonObjectives.l4-a-fine-tuning-run: Fine-tune the tiny GPT for a few steps and measure what it gains and forgets.
lessonObjectives.l5-learning-from-comparisons: Derive the Bradley-Terry model and fit scores from pairwise wins.
lessonObjectives.l6-a-reward-model: Build a reward model as a logistic regression on preference pairs and test it on held-out pairs.
lessonObjectives.l7-reward-on-a-leash: Derive the optimal policy under a KL penalty and compute its reward and divergence.
lessonObjectives.l8-dpo: Derive the DPO loss from the KL-penalised optimum and code it.
lessonObjectives.l9-writing-the-rules-down: Build a critique-and-revise pipeline driven by written principles.
lessonObjectives.l10-feedback-from-a-model: Derive how noisy AI labels shrink a fitted reward gap, and correct for it.
lessonObjectives.l11-many-judges: Code a majority vote of judges and measure and remove position bias.
lessonObjectives.l12-helpful-and-harmless: Measure a model's helpfulness and harmlessness together and explain the trade-off.
lessonObjectives.l13-error-bars: Compute a benchmark score's standard error, including for clustered questions.
lessonObjectives.l14-comparing-two-models: Write a paired comparison of two models on the same questions.
lessonObjectives.l15-has-it-seen-the-test: Code an n-gram overlap check for contamination between training text and a test set.
lessonObjectives.l16-judges-and-many-benchmarks: Correct a model comparison for judge bias and for many benchmarks.
